title: app-shell: the ObjectSchema corpus guards pin an exact top-level key count, so every additive spec change turns Test UI red on main; assert only the membership claims they guard
body:
Filing gate ③: a coordinator-directed structural fix after the main-red of #26218. The maintainer asked whether one red blocking many PRs is the right shape and whether something faster exists. ⛔ Not a claim.

Two app-shell tests pin `Object.keys(ObjectSchema.shape).size` to an exact number:
- `ui/packages/app-shell/src/services/MetadataService.retiredObjectEnabled.test.ts:161`
- `ui/packages/app-shell/src/services/MetadataService.specKeyObjectPayload.test.ts:175`

Each file's own comment block records six re-points (42 → 48). Every one of them was caused by an unrelated spec adoption: `editMode`, `imageField`, `attachedOnRead`, `defaultRowScope`, `membershipKeys`, `sharing`. The count is not what the tests are about. It is described as "the corpus guard for the membership claims below", which are:
- the tombstone keys `enabled` and `_deleted` are refused by name;
- `enable` is the capabilities object;
- no near-spelling of a retired key exists;
- the object payload maps its keys.

The last re-point (#26005 adding `sharing`, fixed by #26218 / #26231) turned Test UI red on every ui PR's merge ref and in the merge queue, and ejected PRs that had nothing to do with it.

**Business reason.** An additive spec change, which is the most common kind, should not stop the ui lane. Today it does, until someone notices and re-points a number.

**Expected.**
- Each guard asserts the claims it exists for, as explicit membership checks.
- No exact count.
- Where the comment says the count backs "no near-spelling of a retired key", that claim is asserted directly over the key set, for example as a no-key-within-edit-distance check against the retired names, rather than through a count.
- The re-point comment history can be condensed to one line that points at this card.
- No product change. Test-only. app-shell is outside the sdui registry closure.

**Related.**
- #26092 closes the other half: the spec PR's CI does not run the ui consumers today (root `turbo.json` / `ci.yml` core filter lines).
- #26222 and #26223 are the bot's aggregation issues for the two files.

**Who acts.** The `domain:ui` seat 2, after #26231 lands, because it edits the same two files.

**Duplicate check.** Searched the 40 newest issues for "corpus guard", "ObjectSchema key count" and "retiredObjectEnabled". Only #26218, #26222 and #26223 came up, all of them about the 48 re-point.
